title: Quantum-geometry transport headroom for finite-lifetime sink capture
purpose: Translate a possible quantum-geometry-driven exciton diffusion enhancement into a conservative sink-capture metric, and quantify how much relative environment/disorder penalty can erase that advantage. This does not reproduce a material-specific topological-exciton calculation or claim a project device has topological excitons.

source_provenance.citation: Thompson et al., Topologically enhanced exciton transport, Nature Communications 16, 11448 (2025)
used_for: topological excitons predicted to enhance transport in free, phonon-limited, and polaronic regimes
up to approximately four-fold transport enhancement in the cited organic polyacene examples
quantum-metric contribution to exciton group velocity/diffusion
proposal to probe exciton quantum geometry with non-uniform electric fields
statement that dielectric environment, chemical modification, and temperature can tune relevant excitonic geometry/topology

source_provenance.citation: Jankowski et al., Excitonic topology and quantum geometry in organic semiconductors, Nature Communications 16, 4661 (2025)
used_for: excitonic topology/quantum-geometry framework in organic semiconductors
topology-related lower bound on exciton centre-of-mass spread

source_provenance.citation: Yu et al., Exciton Steering via Potential Landscape Engineered by Excited Electron-Hole Phase Transition, Physical Review Letters 136, 246901 (2026)
used_for: all-optical reconfigurable exciton steering is experimentally possible in a different 2D material platform

established_external_evidence.topological_exciton_spread_bound: xi^2 >= a^2 P_exc^2 / 4 in the cited 1D inversion-symmetric framework
established_external_evidence.important_boundary: P_exc=0 removes the nonzero topological lower bound but does not imply a trivial exciton has zero size.
established_external_evidence.transport_result_boundary: The approximately 4x transport enhancement is a result of the cited polyacene calculations, not a universal topological factor and not a project measurement.
established_external_evidence.field_probe_boundary: The cited work proposes non-uniform electric-field gradients as a quantum-metric probe; it is not yet a project experiment.

model.geometry: 1D diffusion toward one absorbing sink a distance L away, with independent exponential exciton loss lifetime tau

synthetic_fixture.note: The 4x value is included because it is within the cited polyacene calculation results. It is not assigned to any project material. x is dimensionless and is not a measured device geometry.

independent_verification.analytic_derivation: Solve D u'' - tau^-1 u = 0 with absorbing-sink boundary u(0)=1 and u(infinity)=0.
independent_verification.monte_carlo: Independently sample exact Brownian first-passage time T_hit=L^2/(2 D Z^2), Z~N(0,1), and exponential loss time T_loss~Exp(1/tau); estimate P(T_hit<T_loss).

prospective_branch.name: QG-ENAQT: quantum-geometry x environment co-design
prospective_branch.hypothesis: A material or emulator with a verified quantum-geometric transport contribution can provide diffusion headroom that remains useful under realistic dephasing/phonon/disorder conditions and increases irreversible sink capture without requiring long-lived quantum memory.
prospective_branch.stage_QG0: Reproduce the dimensionless first-passage headroom model and independently reproduce or benchmark a published topological-exciton transport result.
prospective_branch.stage_QG1: Compare a topological candidate and a serious trivial/control system using exciton diffusion imaging; separately measure lifetime so D and tau are not conflated.
prospective_branch.stage_QG2: Apply a calibrated non-uniform electric-field gradient and test the predicted differential transport response while bounding dissociation/free-carrier artifacts.
prospective_branch.stage_QG3: Map temperature, dielectric environment, and controlled disorder/dephasing to test whether the geometric transport advantage persists or collapses.
prospective_branch.stage_QG4: Add an irreversible sink/quencher/electrical extraction boundary at controlled distance and test prospective capture gain against the first-passage prediction.
prospective_branch.future_programmable_extension: Only after QG1-QG4, combine geometry headroom with reconfigurable optical/electric potential landscapes for an exciton router or adaptive sink network.

falsifiers_and_nulls: Matched controls show no diffusion enhancement once exciton lifetime and crystal quality are separated.
The apparent advantage is explained by chemistry, morphology, defects, absorption, or lifetime rather than quantum geometry/topology.
Non-uniform fields primarily dissociate excitons or move free carriers, invalidating the proposed metric interpretation.
Interfaces/defects erase the bulk transport advantage before a useful sink distance is reached.
The candidate's environment/disorder penalty makes rho <= 1/G_intrinsic, eliminating net diffusion headroom.
Higher diffusion does not increase irreversible sink delivery or useful electrical work in the actual geometry.
explicit_non_claims: No project material is claimed to host topological excitons.
No 4x diffusion enhancement is claimed for D18/PY-IT/eC9, PEA2PbI4, or any current device.
The first-passage model is not a full exciton-phonon, polaron, interface, or device simulation.
Topology is not assumed to protect transport from arbitrary disorder or defects.
This is not evidence of quantum computational advantage or fault-tolerant quantum information processing.
